bugs.description: Bot attempted to book with a hallucinated service UUID that the FK validator rejected. This caused the booking to fail. The bot tried to call book tool with a fabricated service_id not present in the DB catalog.

Bot did not ask for the husband's name or treat him as a separate customer entity — it handled both as one booking unit under Mónica's account. This is the known Change M deferred gap: true multi-customer split is not implemented. Bot handled companion as part of same booking, not a separate customer record.

turns.agent_response:
He detectado que se volvió a colar un UUID incorrecto al intentar cerrarla, así que no quiero inventarme nada ni dejarte una reserva mal hecha.

Si quieres, la rehago desde cero correctamente con los dos cortes y te la deja cerrada.

bugs.description: Bot keeps detecting hallucinated UUID on each attempt. Cannot self-recover by re-fetching valid service_ids from catalog. Begins loop: offer redo → try → fail → offer redo.

bugs.description: Second full cycle confirms the bot is stuck in an unrecoverable FK validation loop. It can fetch availability, collect name/policy, but cannot successfully commit a booking for a duo service request without hallucinating service_ids.

Bot hallucinated a service UUID when attempting to book multiple services for a couple. The FK validator in book.py (or update_booking.py) correctly rejected the invalid service_id. Root cause: the LLM fabricates a service UUID when handling multi-service (duo) bookings instead of looking up valid IDs from the catalog via check_availability tool evidence.
bugs.notes: V4 baseline notes this scenario as exercising the FK validator. The validator IS working correctly — it blocks the hallucination. The bug is that the bot cannot self-recover by re-fetching valid service_ids, creating an infinite loop.

bugs.description: After FK validation failure, bot enters an unrecoverable loop: offer redo → attempt with hallucinated UUID → fail → offer redo. Loop persists even after user agrees to restart from scratch (turns 7–12 cover 2 full cycles). Bot never escalates or asks for human help despite being unable to complete the task.
bugs.notes: Known gap — no escalation fallback when book tool fails repeatedly. Bot should escalate after N consecutive booking failures.

bugs.description: Bot handled husband's service as part of Mónica's booking rather than creating a separate customer record for the partner. This is the known Change M deferred gap (true multi-customer split not implemented). Bot asked Mónica's name only, did not ask for husband's name or phone. Companion handling UX: bot treats both services as a single booking for the primary phone holder.
bugs.notes: DEFERRED per scenario instructions — do not report as new bug. Recording for completeness: companion booking UX currently collapses both people's services into one appointment entry under the primary customer.

notes: V6 regression focus: FK validator correctly blocks hallucinated service_ids (validator working as designed since V4). New finding: bot has no self-recovery path after repeated FK failures — it loops indefinitely instead of escalating. Companion handling UX (Change M deferred gap): bot treats both services as one booking under Mónica's account; does not create a separate customer for the partner or ask for his name/phone. The bot DID correctly understand the duo intent, disambiguate services (corte dama vs corte caballero), offer availability, present policy gate, and capture Mónica's name — all pre-commit steps worked. The failure point is exclusively at the book tool call where service_id hallucination occurs.
